controllingContractTextReadDirectly.exactClause: C37 becomes terminal only after its exact commit and normal push are verified.
controllingContractTextReadDirectly.supportingClause: Commit SHA/push/checkpoint-65 facts must be recorded in post-commit attestations rather than invented in a self-referential commit.
controllingContractTextReadDirectly.interpretation: The controlling contract requires exactly two things for terminality: (1) the exact commit exists, and (2) the normal push is verified. It affirmatively supports treating post-commit/post-push attestations (i.e. checkpoint evidence, including this one) as SEPARATE artifacts that need not themselves be committed or pushed for terminality to be reached -- the phrase 'rather than invented in a self-referential commit' exists precisely because the commit cannot contain facts about its own future publication, and the contract resolves that by deferring those facts to subsequent, uncommitted attestations.

adjudicationSelectionNote: Of the five permitted categories (C37_TERMINAL, C37_NONTERMINAL_EVIDENCE_PUBLICATION_PENDING, C37_NONTERMINAL_PUSH_FAILED, C37_NONTERMINAL_POLICY_BLOCKED, C37_SAFE_PAUSE_REMOTE_DIVERGENCE), C37_NONTERMINAL_PUSH_FAILED is the closest fit by its own stated test ('use if the remote branch does not contain the target commit' -- true here). It is applied with an explicit caveat: 'failed' should not be read as a Git-level or server-level rejection. No push was attempted at that level at all; the block occurred one layer higher, in the agent's own tool-permission system. C37_NONTERMINAL_POLICY_BLOCKED was considered and rejected as a label because that category is specifically for identity/signature/repository policy, none of which blocked this push -- the commit identity gate independently cleared as NO_BINDING_IDENTITY_POLICY_FOUND. The remote-observable outcome (commit absent from remote) is identical either way; only the internal cause differs, and that cause is recorded precisely above rather than mislabeled.
